question.headline: Build for sales managers, or resell what already works?
question.asked: My business mentor told me it is easier to sell something that makes people money than something that saves them cost. I sell email agents that save cost. That offer is fully worked out, I know it inside out, and I have two live requests for it right now - it is only harder to sell. My market today is ecommerce, transport and wholesale, on cost saving. The alternative is helping sales managers quote faster and respond faster, which makes them money - but I would have to build the whole product, do the research, and rethink everything for a market I have never sold to. This is my business (Glimps, AI chatbots and agents for small and mid-sized companies in Belgium) and it decides where my revenue comes from. What do I do?

verdict.read: Two live requests and a market you know beats a product you'd have to invent. Transport and wholesale already lose deals on slow quotes - sell them that.

quotes.text: you make another product and then within two or three years all of a sudden you have four mini businesses
not stop doing that. Like if it keeps working, you keep doing it.

call.heading: Stay in your market, sell speed
call.text: Sales managers were never the answer. A transport firm or wholesaler that answers a quote request in minutes wins orders it used to lose. Same agent, same buyers, new promise. Start with your two live requests.

actions.do: Rewrite the two live proposals around orders won
actions.how: Lead with quote speed, keep cost saving as the second reason
actions.detail:
You do not need research for this. You have two people already asking, and you already know what the agent does. What changes is the first line of the proposal.

Right now it opens with hours saved. Open it instead with the order they lost: an enquiry that sat until Thursday while a competitor quoted on Tuesday.

Hormozi's move: the cost saving does not disappear, it moves down the page. It becomes the reason to keep paying, not the reason to buy. Buyers sign for what they gain and renew for what they save.

Send both proposals this week. Nothing to build.

actions.do: Ask both prospects what a slow quote costs
actions.how: One question in the next call, then use their number
actions.detail:
This is the cheapest research you will ever do, and it replaces the market study you were dreading.

Rackham's move: ask how many quote requests came in last month, how many got an answer within the hour, and what an average order is worth. Three questions, one call.

Now you have their arithmetic in their numbers. Twenty late quotes at four thousand euro is eighty thousand on the table, and your price stops being a discussion.

Keenan's move: do not guess the gap for them. Let them say it out loud, then repeat it back in the proposal in their own words.

dissent.text: Blount's point stands: two requests is not a pipeline. Winning both still leaves you with nothing booked for next quarter.
dissent.full:
Blount is not arguing with the call any more. He is arguing with how small it is. Two inbound requests are two conversations, and both could close and you would still be starting next month from zero.

His position: the reframe is free, so do it today, but the real job is outbound into the same three sectors. You now know exactly who to call and exactly what to open with - that is a prospecting list, not a product decision.

Sandler adds the warning: two warm requests are the easiest thing in the world to over-read. If both buy, that proves the story works on people who already came to you. It does not yet prove it works cold.

verdict.vote_label: The vote — each adviser names who should make the call

last_reviewed.note: re-weighed on two live requests and the existing ecom, transport and wholesale market

pn.label: What next
pn.sub: Copy a line into the chat

speeches.name: Alex Hormozi
speeches.text: You have two people asking to buy the thing you already built. That is not the moment to invent a second business for a market you have never sold to. Sales managers were your mentor's example, not your market.

quote.text: you make another product and then within two or three years all of a sudden you have four mini businesses

speeches.name: Dale Carnegie
speeches.text: Carnegie's principle: talk in terms of the other person's interest. A wholesaler does not care about your hours. He cares about the order that went to the competitor who answered first. Same agent, his words.

speeches.name: Jim Keenan
speeches.text: The gap in transport and wholesale is not overhead, it is the quote that goes out too late. You have been selling the cure and describing the wrong disease.

speeches.name: Neil Rackham
speeches.text: Ask what a late quote costs and the problem changes size. That is the whole move. It takes one question in a call you are already having, not a product build.

speeches.name: David Sandler
speeches.text: You have two live requests. Qualify them properly before you rewrite anything. Do they actually lose orders on speed, or did they come to you to cut costs? Do not sell them a story they did not ask for.

speeches.name: Chris Voss
speeches.text: Say it before they can: you probably came to us to cut costs. Then let them tell you what it really costs when nobody answers. Their answer is your proposal.

speeches.name: Jeb Blount
speeches.text: Two requests is two requests. Whatever you call the offer, you are one bad month from an empty pipeline. Ecommerce, transport and wholesale is a list. Go work it.

speeches.name: Jordan Belfort
speeches.text: You believe in this product. That is worth more than the mentor's rule. Do not trade a thing you can sell today for a slide deck about sales managers.

conclusion.label: Where round one landed
conclusion.text: The bench threw out the pivot. The revenue story lives inside the market you already sell to, and your two live requests are where it gets tested.

speeches.name: Jeb Blount
speeches.text: Alex, you are polishing a message for two people. He needs thirty conversations in those three sectors, not two. The wording is a five minute job.

speeches.name: Alex Hormozi
speeches.text: Then it is a five minute job he should do before he makes thirty calls, Jeb. Same effort, better opening line.

speeches.name: David Sandler
speeches.text: And do not read two closed deals as proof. They came to him. A story that works on inbound has not been tested on anyone who was not already looking.

speeches.name: Jim Keenan
speeches.text: Volume without the right diagnosis is thirty polite refusals. He now knows the gap is quote speed. That is what makes the list worth calling.

conclusion.label: Where round two left it
conclusion.text: Nobody defended building for sales managers. The split is only about what comes after the reframe: Blount wants outbound volume, Sandler wants the two requests qualified first.

ballot.why: Two requests is not a pipeline
Speak in the wholesaler's own interest
The gap is quote speed, not overhead
One question resizes the whole problem
Qualify the two before rewriting anything
Volume still beats a better sentence
Their words, not the mentor's frame
Sell what you can already sell

ballot_note: The chair never votes for himself.
